narrative:
The model determined that you have a 60.2% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was denied.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class ranking at the end of your third year was the strongest influence, pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year ranking also pulled the outcome in the same direction, though with less force. These two performance measures outweighed everything else.

Your undergraduate GPA worked in the opposite direction and helped the prediction somewhat, yet it was not enough to overcome the impact of your lower class standings. Compared with students who were admitted, your first-year and third-year deciles placed you at the very bottom of the class (1 versus an average around 6), and your undergraduate GPA of 2.60 sat noticeably below the 3.23 average of successful applicants.

Your LSAT score of 34, lower-middle family income, and plan to attend full-time also contributed to the overall picture, but they played smaller roles than your academic rankings.

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance and consider retaking the LSAT to demonstrate stronger readiness. Strengthening these areas will directly address the factors that most influenced this decision. (218 words)
